title: The Air Show Live at Alaska Investor Day
summary_zh: 本期《The Air Show》在西雅图现场录制，深度复盘阿拉斯加航空投资者日战略，并对话其总裁兼CFO Shane Tackett。核心议题聚焦阿拉斯加航空向全球高端全服务航司的全面转型：申请加入美国航空的跨大西洋及跨太平洋航线联营（JV）、打造配备平躺公务舱与超级经济舱的737 MAX 10跨大陆子机队，以及力争将非主舱收入占比提升至60%。主播Brian与Jon对高油价下每股10美元盈利目标的可行性及高端需求泡沫提出质疑；Shane则坦言2016年拆除维珍美国航空大间距座椅是战略失误，强调机队大型化与高净值客群消费韧性将支撑高端化战略，并详解了放弃国内机队椅背屏幕、全面普及免费Starlink高速Wi-Fi背后的商业权衡。
key_takeaways_zh: 阿拉斯加航空正加速摆脱单一主舱依赖，计划通过常旅客计划（FFP）与高端舱位将非主舱收入占比提升至60%，以抵御高油价等外部成本冲击。
申请加入美国航空的跨大西洋与跨太平洋航线联营（JV）并获取反垄断豁免（ATI），是阿拉斯加航空在缺乏海外根基下支撑西雅图远程宽体机扩张的关键抓手。
复盘收购维珍美国航空后盲目追求座位密度的失误，阿拉斯加航空将于2028年推出25架配备平躺座椅的737 MAX 10子机队重返东西海岸高端跨大陆市场。
面对大型枢纽时刻受限（Slot-controlled）与空域饱和，未来运力增长将转向220至250座级的新一代窄体机以及多发动机供应商竞争模式。
受限于座椅适航取证周期，阿拉斯加航空放弃在国内窄体机加装椅背娱乐屏，转而全面提供免费Starlink高速Wi-Fi以流媒体体验弥补硬件差异。

highlights.title_zh: 投资者日核心发布与市场质疑
highlights.summary_zh: Brett、Brian和Jon盘点了投资者日重磅动作，包括申请加入跨洋航线联营（JV）、推出737 MAX 10平躺跨大陆子机队及宽体机客舱翻新。同时主播们指出，在当前高油价和美联航等对手强力挤压下，其跨大陆航线收益率（Yield）表现与盈利预测面临考验。
highlights.quote_en: So, to me, the biggest news is the application to join the joint ventures: the transatlantic and transpacific joint ventures that American is a part of with its partners.

highlights.title_zh: 油价假设与非主舱增收目标
highlights.summary_zh: 面对Brett关于2.5美元燃油价格假设脱离现实的追问，Shane Tackett回应称航司正通过收入结构转型提升抗风险能力。阿拉斯加航空计划将常旅客计划与高端舱位等主舱以外的收入占比提升至60%，以对冲燃油等成本波动冲击。
highlights.quote_en: What we firmly believe in and why we announced what we did today, more of our revenue needs to come from outside the main cabin.

highlights.summary_zh: 针对近期737 MAX 10软件适航取证波折，Shane表示首批188座构型仍维持春末交付预期，且2028年投运的25架高端跨大陆子机队进度不受影响。若交付推迟，航司可通过延缓老旧飞机退役或提高现有机队利用率灵活应对。
highlights.quote_en: If for whatever reason we didn't get them in the timeframe we thought they were coming, we could extend some of the aircraft we were planning to retire.

highlights.title_zh: 复盘维珍失误与高端需求韧性
highlights.summary_zh: Shane罕见承认2016年拆除维珍美国航空头等舱大间距座椅、转向高密度布局在加州至纽约市场是错误决策。他认为高净值客群可支配收入的强劲增长及大机型带来的客舱精细化分层，使高端出行需求具备跨越周期的粘性。
highlights.quote_en: And what we've actually seen in that particular market, California to New York, is that didn't end up being the right decision.

highlights.title_zh: 联手美航闯关跨洋联营审批
highlights.summary_zh: 针对两家美国本土航司共同参与跨洋航线联营（JV）的监管难点，Shane强调美国航空并未涉足西雅图远程国际市场，双方的合作实质是为西雅图带来增量运力与市场竞争。获取反垄断豁免（ATI）将为阿拉斯加航空庞大的宽体机储备订单（Backlog）提供商业支撑。
highlights.quote_en: We're bringing new capacity to a market that that other partner wasn't serving, didn't have an interest to serve.

highlights.title_zh: 呼吁更大窄体机与发动机竞争
highlights.summary_zh: 鉴于大型枢纽机场时刻与容量趋于饱和，Shane指出未来增长无法再靠加密班次，必须依靠单机大型化，并期待波音未来推出220至250座级新机型。吸取近年发动机维保成本飙升的教训，他呼吁下一代机型引入多家发动机供应商竞争机制以分散风险。
highlights.quote_en: I would love, you know, something in the, I don't know, 220 to 250 range ultimately. It's a long time off, but, yeah, I do think that that is the way that we're going to be able to grow over time, not through frequency.

highlights.title_zh: 放弃椅背屏与普及高速卫星网
highlights.summary_zh: 不同于美国航空等竞争对手重新加装椅背屏幕，Shane解释称带屏座椅的适航审批周期过长，会拖累2028年完成客舱改造的整体进度。客户调研与净推荐值（NPS）显示，旅客更看重稳定不断网的免费Starlink高速Wi-Fi来观看个人设备流媒体。
highlights.quote_en: Our Net Promoter Scores on the flights and equipment that have Starlink are meaningfully higher than the ones that don't, just for that fact that they have Starlink.

transcript.en: Just curious, are they going to make that profit target?

transcript.en: So, to me, the biggest news uh is the application to join the joint ventures: the transatlantic and transpacific joint ventures that American is a part of with its partners. That is a huge deal if it happens.
transcript.zh: 在我看来，最大的新闻是他们申请加入航线联营（JV）——也就是美航与其合作伙伴所在的跨大西洋和跨太平洋航线联营。如果真能成行，那将意义重大。

transcript.en: Well, that is true, but it requires antitrust regulators in other places to approve as well. So...

transcript.en: We do have that problem. But we will ask Shane about this.

Premium reserve, so creating the premium economy product was was certainly newsworthy.

transcript.en: The uh Leihoku redo on the A330 fleet, long overdue renovation on that. Uh we have uh the lounges, which we knew were coming in Seattle, Honolulu, and San Diego, but now we know what they're going to look like, and pizza ovens or something?

transcript.zh: 好的。客舱产品方面的大多数动作其实都在我意料之中。夏威夷航空早就透露过会升级 A330 的套房舱，我也预感到了梦想客机会有新动作，毕竟后续还有那么多新机要交付。我万万没想到的是，他们居然会为 737 MAX 搞一个平躺座椅子机队。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: This is a jar here that that that Jon made, and we have quarters. For people in the back that can't see it, it says Kirby. Look, I don't know if they've heard this before, but Mr. Kirby, CEO of United, says that if you're not first, you're last.
transcript.zh: 这是 Jon 做的一个罚款罐，里面装了硬币。坐在后排看不清的观众，罐子上写着“Kirby”（美联航 CEO）。虽然不知道大家以前听没听过，但美联航首席执行官 Kirby 先生曾说过：如果你不是第一，那你就是倒数第一。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And so, you know, by my count, what they'll be the fifth airline with flat beds going across the country? I mean, not to say that this isn't a bad idea, this is what people in California, in New York, and other coastal markets want. But we have United, which is very very aggressive, they're planning to have 50 Coastliners, which are essentially the same thing.
transcript.zh: 所以按我的计算，他们会是全美第 5 家在跨大陆航线上配备平躺座椅的航司吧？我倒不是说这是个坏主意，加州、纽约和其他沿海市场的旅客确实需要这个。但美联航的攻势极其凶猛，他们正计划引进 50 架‘Coastliner’，本质上也是完全一样的配置。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Those folks at United mean business. I look forward to seeing what Alaska can do with these MAXs, but I know that I'll be flying them a lot because my understanding is that they're going to be flying from LA to Newark, and I think we know they're going to be the cheapest option in the market.
transcript.zh: 美联航的那帮人可是动真格的。我很期待看到阿拉斯加航空用这些 MAX 能玩出什么花样，但我知道自己肯定会经常坐，因为据我了解它们将执飞洛杉矶到纽瓦克的航线，而且大家心知肚明，他们家绝对会是市场上最便宜的选择。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: We know they're flying from LA to undisclosed Newark...
transcript.zh: 我们知道他们会从洛杉矶飞往尚未官宣的纽瓦克……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I'm going to tell you Newark, man. I'm going to tell you Newark four times a day, that's my prediction. I don't know where I got that prediction, but it's a good prediction.
transcript.zh: 我敢断定就是纽瓦克，伙计。我猜每天四班纽瓦克，这是我的预言。我也不知道我怎么得出这个预测的，但这绝对靠谱。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Wow. Yeah. Okay. All right.
transcript.zh: 哇哦。行吧。好吧。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I like to know what's happening in my local market.
transcript.zh: 我向来喜欢摸清自己本地市场的一举一动。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: So, how epic is the yield destruction going to be here?
transcript.zh: 那么，这里的收益率崩盘会有多么惊心动魄呢？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: You want to ask Shane that?
transcript.zh: 你想拿这个问题问 Shane 吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: No, I mean, this is the question we'll ask Shane, right? If this premium boom goes on forever, then it'll be okay. I mean, there were a lot of people that questioned whether there was room for JetBlue in this market. It turned out that there was, they got in actually pretty early on the premium booms. How long is this going to last? Does anybody in the audience know how long it's going to last?
transcript.zh: 不，我是说这正是我们要问 Shane 的核心问题，对吧？如果这场高端舱位繁荣永远持续下去，那自然不成问题。此前也有很多人质疑这个市场是否容得下捷蓝航空（JetBlue），事实证明完全容得下，而且他们实际上很早就踩准了高端出行的风口。但这股浪潮究竟能持续多久？现场观众里有谁知道它能撑多久吗？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Well, look, I think the one thing you can always count on with the American economy is that booms go on forever. There's never any question about...
transcript.zh: 哎，你看，关于美国经济你永远可以确信的一点，就是繁荣永远不会落幕。关于这一点从来没有任何疑虑……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Well, Jon, I think the other thing we know is that this time is different.
transcript.zh: 好吧，Jon，我觉得我们深知的另一件事是：这次不一样。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Oh, no, it's always different. Oh, it's definitely different.
transcript.zh: 噢不，每次都“不一样”。对，这次绝对不一样。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: We'll never lose money again. All right. Jon, since there was no real metal news to
transcript.zh: 我们再也不会亏钱了。好吧。Jon，既然今天没有什么真正的造飞机硬件大新闻……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: talk about, what was most interesting here?
transcript.zh: 探讨的内容，你觉得今天最值得关注的是什么？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Well, look, I kind of felt like the oil stuff was... like if I had a horn, I'd be a unicorn? Yeah. It's like if oil were $2.50, you know, you'd be making 10X EBITDA or whatever.
transcript.zh: 这个嘛，听着，我觉得油价那套假设有点空中楼阁，就像说“我要是长了角，我就是独角兽”一样？对。就像如果油价跌到2.5美元，你的EBITDA就能翻十倍之类的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: $10 EPS. Thank you. Yeah. Yeah, EPS.
transcript.zh: 是每股收益（EPS）达到10美元。多谢提醒。对，每股收益。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: And so it's a lot of baked-in assumptions for a world that, you know, was in the past. And so yes, I think that the one thing that we've seen consistently is that oil is staying high. You know, I don't think the world is getting, sadly, any more stable than it is. And so, you know, do these assumptions hold? And ultimately, has oil wiped out a lot of this? But at the same time, I also think you kind of have to grow to survive it. You need to generate more revenue just to keep the strategy operating.
transcript.zh: 所以这里面夹杂了大量基于过去旧常态的固有预设。事实也的确如此，我们一直看到油价始终居高不下。遗憾的是，我认为世界局势并没有变得更稳定。所以说，这些假设真的站得住脚吗？归根结底，高油价是否已经把大部分预期利润给冲销掉了？但与此同时，我也认为你必须通过扩张来求生存。你必须创造更多营收，才能维持这套战略运转。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Jon, can you imagine how much money they're losing on the Seoul route right now? Well, I don't know.
transcript.zh: Jon，你能想象他们现在的首尔航线上亏了多少钱吗？这我还真说不准。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: For me, the joint venture piece was the biggest news. Because for Alaska, they're trying to build a long-haul network from scratch with 430 jet fuel, and that is very hard. But you know what makes it easy? A joint venture with several of the leading airlines over the Atlantic and the Pacific. I think that is a huge, huge change that I just wonder if it gets through.
transcript.zh: 对我来说，航线联营（JV）才是最大的新闻。因为对阿拉斯加航空而言，要在航油价格4.30美元的高位下白手起家搭建远程国际航线网络，那是极其困难的。但你知道什么能让这事变容易吗？那就是在大西洋和太平洋航线上与几家头部航司建立联营。我认为这是一个巨大的、颠覆性的转变，但我只是怀疑这能不能通过审批。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Do you know a lot of European regulators that we can talk to?
transcript.zh: 你认识很多能说得上话的欧洲监管机构官员吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I don't. Do you?
transcript.zh: 我不认识。你认识？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I don't.
transcript.zh: 我也不认识。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: You might.
transcript.zh: 说不定你真认识呢。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: No, not in Japan either, so it's really hard to know, right? Yeah.
transcript.zh: 不，日本那边的我也不熟，所以这事真的很难说，对吧？是啊。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Well, I have questions for Shane on this one. But this is probably a good place to stop, and we will be bringing out Alaska's President and CFO Shane Tackett. But first, let's take a quick break.
transcript.zh: 好吧，关于这点我有问题要问Shane。不过现在差不多该告一段落了，接下来我们将请出阿拉斯加航空总裁兼首席财务官Shane Tackett。但在那之前，我们先进一段插播广告。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: We have Alaska Airlines' president...
transcript.zh: 我们有请阿拉斯加航空总裁……

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: And Chief Financial Officer Shane Tackett, come on down!
transcript.zh: 还有首席财务官Shane Tackett，快请上台！

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Are you taking collections for Kirby or?
transcript.zh: 你们这是在为Kirby募捐吗？还是什么情况？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: No, if you mention Scott Kirby's name, you have to put a quarter in the jar.
transcript.zh: 不是，只要你提到Scott Kirby的名字，就得往罐子里塞两毛五分钱。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I did I did bring something that I could put in the collection jar if we wanted to.
transcript.zh: 我确实带了点东西，要是需要的话可以投进募捐罐里。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Oh, what do you got? I just have money. Like, isn't that what it's for?
transcript.zh: 哦，你带了什么？我带了钱啊。难道不就是用来装钱的吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah, that's for We usually do a quarter in the jar thing. Clearly, you don't actually listen to the show. It's It's a bit that we do.
transcript.zh: 对，那就是用来……我们通常是往罐子里投两毛五。显然你平时根本不听我们的节目，这是我们节目的一个保留梗。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: No, it's hard to hear back there.
transcript.zh: 不是，在后台实在听不太清楚。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: No, I mean every week we do this bit.
transcript.zh: 不，我是说我们每周都会玩这个梗。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Shane's like, "We're spending all this money. I don't care." It's more for everybody. Let's go.
transcript.zh: Shane心想：“反正我们花了这么多钱，我才不在乎呢。”见者有份，发钱啦！

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: All right. All right. Shane, thank you for joining us.
transcript.zh: 好的。好的。Shane，非常感谢你的到来。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I, um The most important question I have: Is Long Beach the best performing station at Alaska, or the second best? Cuz this is...
transcript.zh: 我……我最关键的问题是：长滩（LGB）是阿拉斯加航空表现最好的航站，还是第二好的？因为这……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett, how many people were in your flight yesterday?
transcript.zh: Brett，你昨天的航班上有多少乘客？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: No one. Listen, it's fine. I don't need an answer. I know.
transcript.zh: 一个人都没有。听着，没关系，我不需要回答，我自己心里有数。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Brett got a private charter.
transcript.zh: Brett等于包了架专机。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: It's our It's our It's our best new again market. It's our best new again market.
transcript.zh: 这是我们……这是我们重开的航线中表现最好的新市场，绝对是重开航线里的佼佼者。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: No, no. My My real question here: So, you know, you had slides up there today. At $2.50 a gallon, you guys are making $10 earnings per share, right?
transcript.zh: 不不，言归正传，我真正想问的是：今天你在幻灯片里展示了，在燃油每加仑2.5美元时，你们能实现每股收益10美元，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Uh, but that was your plan before, and so now fuel is higher. We hear a lot of airlines that are talking about, well, we're able to recapture revenue, you know, over the last few months we've been able to raise our fares, get up there.
transcript.zh: 额，但那是你们之前的预期规划，而现在的油价更高了。我们听到很多航司都在讲，过去几个月他们能够拉回收益，能够提高票价迎头赶上。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: This kind of makes it sound like you guys are are not necessarily having the same luck, right? If you're still saying we need to be at $2.50 a gallon to hit that $10 earnings level, are you are you not having the same ability to recapture revenue as as others are, or am I just reading this wrong?
transcript.zh: 这听起来感觉你们好像并没有那么幸运，对吧？如果你依然坚持说油价必须降到每加仑2.5美元才能达到10美元的每股收益水平，是你们没能像其他航司那样具备拉回收益的能力，还是我解读错了？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: First, I like my spreadsheet a lot at $2.50. So, you know, we wanted to talk about it because it, you know, it would be a a a fun day when when that happens again.
transcript.zh: 首先，我非常喜欢燃油在2.5美元时模型跑出来的数据。所以，我们今天拿出来讨论是因为，有朝一日油价重回那个水平确实会让人很开心。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Um, no, I don't think our story is a whole lot different, to be honest. Um, I do think there's a couple of airlines that are probably doing better than everybody else.
transcript.zh: 额，不过说实话，我认为我们的情况与其他航司并没有太大差异。当然，确实有那么一两家航司的业绩表现可能优于行业平均水平。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And I think we do have a hypothesis on why, and a lot of that is what we started to talk about in 2024. And cynics or no, what we firmly believe in and why we announced what we did today, more of our revenue needs to come from outside the main cabin.
transcript.zh: 对于其中的原因，我们确实有一套假说，很大程度上也是我们在2024年就开始探讨的东西。不管外界如何质疑，我们对此坚信不疑，这也是我们今天公布这一举措的原因：我们需要让更多的收入来自于普通经济舱之外。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: If you look at the last several years, you guys watch the industry as much as anybody, where there has been absolute revenue growth, certainly unit revenue growth, it's been in areas outside the main cabin. It's been from loyalty and, and then in the premium cabins, we've seen that.
transcript.zh: 纵观过去几年，你们对行业的关注不输任何人，真正的绝对收入增长——尤其是单位收入增长，全都来自于普通经济舱之外的领域。它们来自常旅客计划，以及我们所见证的高端舱位。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I think whether it's durable or not, we can talk about. But that's why we shared our goal, ultimately, of getting to 60% of the revenues outside of the main cabin.
transcript.zh: 这种增长是否具备可持续性，我们还可以讨论。但这就是为什么我们提出了最终目标：让60%的收入来自于普通经济舱之外。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: When you do that, you're more able to, I think, withstand any sort of industry shock, including a big input price shock.
transcript.zh: 只要做到了这一点，我认为航司就更有能力抵御任何形式的行业冲击，包括核心生产要素价格暴涨的巨大冲击。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: To the business model. The reason we did that, and I'll be short after this, really was because we had made that commitment and expectation two years ago. We felt like if we're going to bring investors in, we have to go talk about the $10 again.
transcript.zh: 转向这种商业模式。我们之所以这么做——后面我会长话短说——确实是因为我们在两年前做出了这项承诺并设定了预期。我们觉得既然要召集投资者，就必须再次跟他们把这10美元谈清楚。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And I think it's super clear to us that the strategy is the right strategy. A lot of things are working well. Nothing ever is linear, it doesn't work exactly the way we had expected or planned it to.
transcript.zh: 而且我认为在我们看来非常明确的是，这项战略是完全正确的。很多业务进展顺利。事情从来都不是线性发展的，不可能完全按照我们预期或计划的轨道推进。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: But, as fuel normalizes, earnings are going to go in the right direction, and I think they'll go pretty quickly.
transcript.zh: 但是，随着燃油价格回归常态，盈利水平将朝着正确的方向发展，而且我认为回升速度会相当快。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And when is that happening?
transcript.zh: 那具体会在什么时候发生呢？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I heard after the midterms. I don't know, did you not hear the same? That's what I heard.
transcript.zh: 我听说是在中期选举之后。我不知道，你们听到的不是这样吗？反正我听到的是这样。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: We try not to do politics on the show.
transcript.zh: 我们节目尽量不聊政治。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Thank you. Let's not do any more of those. Let's not do any more of those.
transcript.zh: 感谢。咱们可别再提那些了，坚决别再聊那个话题了。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: No, it's fine though. But after midterms, he guaranteed it, so we're good.
transcript.zh: 没事儿，不过中期选举后他可是打包票了，所以咱们放宽心就好。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: There we go. Hey, look, if we don't force an 8-K out of this conversation, we have done something wrong. I'm just saying.
transcript.zh: 这就对了。嘿，听着，如果我们今天这场对话没逼得你们发一份8-K重大事项公告，那肯定是我们没发挥好。我只是开个玩笑。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: If you do, I've done something wrong and I'm going to pay for it.
transcript.zh: 要是真逼出来了，那肯定是我说错话了，我得为此背锅。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: You know, it wouldn't be the first time today that they rushed an 8-K out, or you made an 8-K mistake. We were told you were going to announce the joint venture after the market closed today. It went out in the morning.
transcript.zh: 要知道，这可不是你们今天头一回急急忙忙发8-K公告，或者犯8-K信披失误了。我们之前得到的消息是，你们本打算在今天美股收盘后宣布航线联营（JV）的消息，结果一大早就发出来了。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Technically, we did release our joint press release at 1:00 p.m. That's when we did announce it.
transcript.zh: 从严格意义上讲，我们的联合新闻稿确实是在下午1点发布的。那才是我们正式官宣的时间。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Oh, you're referring to the slide in our deck that got issued with the 8-K that might have hinted at it? "Hinted" is a strong word. It might have been a bit bad, but we're doing it.
transcript.zh: 噢，你指的是我们随8-K公告一起发出的演示文稿幻灯片里有所暗示？说“暗示”未免太委婉了。确实可能有点尴尬，但总之我们已经在推进了。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Look, I can't help myself, I want to ask about airplanes. MAX 10s obviously back in the news. This week ostensibly was supposed to be the certification of the MAX 10, the airplane that's going to make Sea-Tac work for you guys on upgauging.
transcript.zh: 听着，我实在忍不住，我还是想聊飞机。737 MAX 10显然又重回新闻焦点了。本周表面上原本应该是MAX 10完成适航取证的节点，而这款飞机正是你们在西雅图-塔科马机场推行机型升级放大（upgauging）的关键运力支撑。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: We've got obviously a glitch with software certification pop up kind of the last minute here. You've got 25 airplanes that you've earmarked in 2028 for premium transcon. Your first two 188-seat MAX 10s are currently coming down the line in Renton.
transcript.zh: 显而易见，软件适航认证在最后一刻出了一点故障纰漏。你们已经专门指定了25架飞机计划在2028年投放到高端跨陆航线上。你们首批两架188座布局的MAX 10目前正在伦顿总装线下线。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: What is your understanding of when you're actually going to be getting these airplanes, and how are you preparing for more uncertainty around the delivery?
transcript.zh: 据你了解，你们究竟何时才能真正接收这些飞机？面对交付方面进一步增加的不确定性，你们又在做怎样的准备？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Sure. And Jon, I love how you catch little details and describe them as our whole strategy. I think Sea-Tac is going to work without the MAX 10 alone, but it's certainly going to be a big help for us over the years, and we're excited to get the airplane.
transcript.zh: 没问题。Jon，我很佩服你总能捕捉到细枝末节并把它们概括成我们的全盘战略。我认为就算没有MAX 10，西雅图-塔科马的业务也运转得下去，但未来几年它确实能给我们提供巨大助力，我们非常期待接收这款飞机。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Yeah, we have a couple due to us in March, April time frame, and then sort of ratably throughout the year. We want the airplanes. We've been talking about the airplanes for a couple of years.
transcript.zh: 是的，我们有几架预计在3月到4月期间交付，随后全年在各个阶段按节奏逐步接收。我们非常需要这些飞机，关于它们我们已经谈论好几年了。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Our biggest order ever we made was really underpinned by the airplane: 105 MAX 10s plus the five 787s. We are anxious to ultimately get them into the fleet and fly them, but we...
transcript.zh: 我们有史以来签署的最大规模订单，其核心支柱就是这款飞机：105架MAX 10加上5架787。我们非常渴望最终能将它们编入机队投入商业运营，但是我们……

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: ...are going to stand on the side and let the certification process take care of itself. I think what...
transcript.zh: ……我们打算静观其变，让适航取证程序按部就班地进行。我认为……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Is there another option? Is there another option? Like jump in there?
transcript.zh: 难道还有别的选择吗？还能有别的选择？比如亲自插手进去？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: We are not... We are not going to be pushing the certification process on our end at all. We would never do that. Safety is the most important thing.
transcript.zh: 我们绝对不会……从航司端去催促适航审定进度，我们绝不会那么做。安全始终是重中之重。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: The process is meant to go find issues and then resolve issues, so I think the process is working. We don't have an updated timeline. We haven't been told that the aircraft will be delayed beyond March, so we don't have a reason to talk about a different date.
transcript.zh: 这个程序的意义本就是发现问题并解决问题，因此我认为审定流程正在正常发挥作用。我们目前没有更新的时间表。我们尚未收到飞机交付会推迟到三月份之后的通知，所以我们也没理由去谈论其他日期。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I certainly think that we feel very confident that the premium version of those that are meant to come in 2028, lots of confidence that that's still on track. There's a lot of other certifications with seats and other things that we have to do on the LOPA, which you understand well, Jon.
transcript.zh: 但我可以肯定地说，我们对计划于2028年交付的高端客舱构型版本非常有信心，坚信它仍按部就班推进。当然在机舱布局（LOPA）上，我们在座椅等方面还有很多其他审定工作要做，Jon对此肯定很清楚。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And if for whatever reason we didn't get them in the timeframe we thought they were coming, we could extend some of the aircraft we were planning to retire, or we could fly some of the other fleets a little harder.
transcript.zh: 如果出于某种原因，新机未能如期交付，我们也可以顺延部分原定退役飞机的服役期，或者加大其他现有机队的执飞强度。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: So the thing about airlines in general, these new fleets, they take a while to become a big part of what you're doing. They don't mean that much in terms of our total growth next year. And one thing we've become pretty good at over the last several years is moving around delivery horizon for lots of different reasons. So we can adapt pretty quickly.
transcript.zh: 对航司而言，新机队通常需要一段时间才能在运营中挑起大梁。它们对我们明年的整体运力增长影响有限。而在过去几年里，我们已经非常擅长因各种原因调整交付周期，因此我们的应变速度会非常快。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: All right Shane, you told us that we could talk about the durability of premium. I'd like to do that. We made a joke when you were standing back there, right, that you all say that this time is different and it's a cycle that's going to go on forever.
transcript.zh: 好的Shane，你刚才说我们可以聊聊高端客舱需求的持久性。我很想探讨这个话题。刚才你站在后面时我们还开玩笑说，你们总是宣称‘这次不一样’，而且这种行情周期会一直持续下去。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But in a world where Frontier apparently is getting first class, and JetBlue is doing first class, and actually Allegiant too, give us an honest answer here: why do you guys say like this is going to last forever?
transcript.zh: 但在如今连Frontier似乎都要配头等舱、JetBlue也在做头等舱、甚至连Allegiant都要搞头等舱的世道下，给我们一句交底的实话：你们凭什么认为这种热潮能一直持续？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: In fact, at Investor Day today, you basically told people that the last cycle that ended, it was all about low cost, right? It was all about the commodity and then that ended. Why is this one not going to end? It's been going on for what, 20 years?
transcript.zh: 事实上，在今天的投资者日上，你基本上也是跟外界表示，上一轮已经终结的周期完全是由低成本驱动的，对吧？当时拼的全是大宗普通出行产品，然后那个周期落幕了。为什么这一轮周期就不会终结呢？它已经持续了多久，20年了吗？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Yeah, but because you just admitted you're going to be on the airplane.
transcript.zh: 对，但正如你刚才亲口承认的，你依然会去坐飞机。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: But did you hear the other part about that? It's because it's going to be cheap.
transcript.zh: 但你听清我后面那半句了吗？那是因为机票便宜我才坐啊。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Look, I think it's... I grew up in the industry, you guys have watched it for a long time. I think, like I'll admit, in 2016 I was asked, you know, about the front of the cabin for Virgin.
transcript.zh: 听我说，我觉得……我在这个行业摸爬滚打长大，你们也长期观察这个行业。其实我坦白讲，在2016年时就有人问过我关于Virgin前舱布局的问题。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And we made the decision at the time to take I think they were 54-inch pitch seats off, white leather, they were beautiful, and ultimately remodel those aircraft to look like our interiors that we had at Alaska. And our thesis was the density was the better play.
transcript.zh: 当时我们决定拆掉那些座椅间距据说有54英寸的白色皮质座椅——它们确实很漂亮——并将那些飞机彻底改装成符合我们Alaska客舱内饰的风格。我们当时的逻辑是，提高客舱座位密度才是更优解。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And what we've actually seen in that particular market, California to New York...
transcript.zh: 而我们在那个特定市场，也就是加利福尼亚飞纽约航线上所亲眼见证的……

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: ...is that didn't end up being the right decision.
transcript.zh: ……但这最终并不是一个正确的决定。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Listen, an airline executive who admitted he was wrong.
transcript.zh: 听听，一位承认自己做错了的航司高管。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Admits, yeah.
transcript.zh: 确实承认了，是的。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I think that if you look at those markets, we have underperformed the rest of the industry. And the reason is we didn't have the right asset.
transcript.zh: 我认为如果仔细审视那些市场，我们的表现确实不如行业内其他航司。原因就在于我们没有配置合适的机型资产。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And I don't know if that was a precursor to kind of the hypothesis we've all ended up developing today, but it's really clear there are markets, there are pockets of demand, and I think those pockets of demand are growing, where the experience matters as much as the other side of the trip. The aircraft, the experience with the airline matters as much as where people are going.
transcript.zh: 我不知道这是否算我们如今普遍得出的这个假设的前兆，但显而易见的是，确实存在某些细分市场和特定需求，而且这种需求还在不断增长——即飞行体验与旅途目的地同样重要。飞机本身以及航司提供的出行体验，其重要性已经不亚于旅客去往的目的地。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: So they want to start their trip in a premium lounge and then in a premium cabin and then go to wherever they're going to enjoy a vacation or whatever.
transcript.zh: 所以他们希望从高端休息室开始他们的旅程，接着进入高舱等客舱，然后再抵达目的地去享受度假之类的行程。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And we don't think that things only move up and to the right, you know, for all of our lives. What we do think is people who are traveling increasingly want a better experience.
transcript.zh: 我们并不认为这种趋势在我们有生之年会一直直线上升。但我们确信的是，出门旅行的人越来越渴望获得更优质的体验。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Turns out that the idea that everybody wanted as little legroom as you could possibly get, with no amenities, and not very good food and beverage, and no Wi-Fi, and no other things to make you comfortable, isn't really what people want. People want the best experience that they can afford.
transcript.zh: 事实证明，那种认为所有人都只想尽量压缩腿部空间、不需要任何便利设施、不在乎餐饮品质、没有Wi-Fi以及缺乏任何舒适配置的理念，根本就不是旅客真正想要的。人们想要的是自己在经济能力承受范围内最好的体验。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And I think with larger aircraft, we're able to produce more of these premium experience at a price point that people can afford. And I don't know, Brian, like in your life, for Jon and Brett, like do you typically go and do something that you feel is like really nice and treated yourself and then want to trade down later? And I just don't think most people want to do that.
transcript.zh: 我认为换用更大的飞机后，我们能够以大家负担得起的价格，提供更多这种高端体验。而且我不知道，Brian，包括Jon和Brett，在你们的生活中，你们是否经常在犒劳自己享受了一次非常美好的体验之后，转头又想降级去选更差的？我觉得大多数人都不愿意这样消费降级。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Now, you know, if the economy goes into a big downturn, yeah, I think all airlines are going to have to deal with that, and they're not going to see an up-only sort of premium demand pool. But I do think there's going to be more ability to find out if those pockets of demand are more resilient than folks who really have to be much more focused on the price.
transcript.zh: 当然，如果经济陷入严重衰退，所有航司都必须面对这种局面，高端客源需求池也绝不可能只涨不跌。但我确实认为，届时我们更有机会去验证，这类高端细分需求是否会比那些对价格极度敏感的客群更具韧性。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Well, I think this is really interesting because you just hit on something that's really, I think, key here. When we talk about AI, I think everyone sort of agrees, you ask Jeff Bezos, he's like, 'Well, is AI a bubble?' He's like, 'Well, it doesn't really matter because we're going to be left with all of these data centers that are going to have all of this compute power and that we can use for something else on the other side of this economic revolution.'
transcript.zh: 我认为这非常有意思，因为你刚才恰好切中了这里非常关键的核心。当谈到AI时，大家似乎都有共识，如果你去问Jeff Bezos‘AI存在泡沫吗？’他会回答说：‘这其实并不重要，因为这场经济变革之后，我们将留下所有这些数据中心，拥有所有的算力，并且可以将其转用于其他用途。’

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Okay. So if the premium bubble bursts, we're going to be left with a whole lot of premium seats in the system. As you model that, I mean, when you lay in bed at night thinking about sort of the things that worry you about either the durability of this or what comes after, what do you think about?
transcript.zh: 那么好，如果两舱高端泡沫破裂，整个民航系统里将留下大量的高端舱位。在你们进行财务和收益建模时，我是说，当你深夜躺在床上思考那些让你担忧的问题——无论是这种趋势的持续性，还是泡沫破裂后的烂摊子——你脑海里都在想些什么？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Jon, I want to know what you think about when you lay in bed at night, because it's probably not when the premium bubble bursts. But yes, I understand.
transcript.zh: Jon，我倒很想知道你深夜躺在床上都在想些什么，估计多半不是两舱高端泡沫什么时候破裂吧。不过是的，我明白你的意思。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: I hope you are actually, you know...
transcript.zh: 我希望你其实也在思考……

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: DJ, I understand. I don't...
transcript.zh: DJ，我懂。我倒不……

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: You guys may not buy this, but, um, like when I started at the airline, I think our average gauge was around 140 seats, right? And we had First Class, we didn't really have anything behind First Class. Everything else was just sort of standard Main Cabin.
transcript.zh: 你们可能不信，但我刚加入这家航司时，我们的平均座级大概只有140座左右，对吧？当时我们有头等舱，但头等舱后面基本就没什么细分产品了，剩下的全都是标准经济舱。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And First Class was primarily, you guys know this story, was an upgrade product. The MAX 10 is going to be 188 seats. I think we have plenty of Main Cabin seats in the aircraft.
transcript.zh: 而且头等舱在过去——你们都知道这回事——主要是作为升舱产品存在的。而MAX 10将配置188个座位。我认为这架飞机上有足够多的经济舱座位。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And the one thing I do know is increasingly people want to know where they're sitting and they want to choose where they're sitting. And we haven't gone as far as other airlines in terms of monetizing that. Lots of other airlines are selling a standard Main Cabin seat, you know, far back behind the exit row or something like that.
transcript.zh: 我确切知道的一点是，越来越多的旅客希望清楚自己的具体座位，并希望能自主选座。在利用这一点进行创收方面，我们还没有像其他航司走得那么激进。很多其他航司甚至连应急出口后方深处的标准经济舱座位都要拿来加价售卖。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: We haven't gone that far. But people really want to know what their experience is going to be like, and they're willing to pay a few extra dollars for that. And so, even if there's an economic downturn and people aren't able to spend what they do today on premium, I think there's almost always a 100% demand for First Class or a 100% demand for lie-flat, right?
transcript.zh: 我们还没做到那一步。但旅客确实非常在意自己的乘机体验，并且愿意为此多花几块钱。因此，即便经济出现下行，人们无法像今天这样在高端客舱上一掷千金，我认为市场上对头等舱或平躺座椅的需求几乎永远是100%存在的，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Everybody on the plane would like to be up there.
transcript.zh: 飞机上的每个人都希望能坐到前面去。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah, at what price?
transcript.zh: 是啊，但看是什么票价了。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: So yes, it does come down to yields. I do understand that. So I do think the larger-format planes have allowed airlines to segment their products like almost every other industry tries to do in a way that's more successful.
transcript.zh: 没错，这归根结底取决于收益率，这点我非常清楚。所以，我认为更大规格的机型让航司能够像其他各行各业一样进行产品细分，而且是以一种更为成功的方式来实现。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And I do think it is different because a lot of the assets we're using are different. And I will say this, and I think, Brian, you may or may not agree, I do think if you take the most premium part of the market, people who are able to pay for the most premium experiences, I do think that their growth in discretionary income has vastly outpaced the price of living in a way that's different than a lot of the rest of the customers that we serve.
transcript.zh: 我也确实认为如今情况有所不同，因为我们使用的很多资产都不同了。另外我想说——Brian，你可能同意也可能不同意——我认为从市场最顶端的高端客群来看，即那些有能力为最顶尖体验买单的人，其可支配收入的增长速度远远跑赢了生活成本，这与我们服务的大多数普通旅客是截然不同的。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: To a degree where it may be that that demand is more sticky over time. But we're going to have to go live a few more years to see if I'm right or not.
transcript.zh: 这种差距甚至使得高端需求随着时间推移展现出更强的黏性。不过我们还得再过几年才能验证我说的到底对不对。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: All right, I want to get a little more specific on this because I was kind of jonesing for some network news today. And I don't know, for those of you who were there, there was this great visual of this route map, and it showed Seattle, Portland, San Francisco, LA, San Diego, and it had lines on it.
transcript.zh: 好的，我想针对这一点聊得更具体些，因为我今天特别渴望听到一些航线网络方面的新闻。不知道大家注意到没有，当时现场展示了一张非常棒的航线网络图，上面标着西雅图、波特兰、旧金山、洛杉矶和圣迭戈，航线纵横交错。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: And then it started panning over to the East Coast, and you're like, "Where's it going to end?" And then it was just like a gray, blue, whatever area in the Northeast, and it just stopped.
transcript.zh: 然后镜头开始向东海岸平移，大家都在想：“这航线会在哪儿停呢？”结果到了美东东北部，就只是一片灰蓝色区域，然后戛然而止。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: A glow.
transcript.zh: 就一片光晕。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: It was so I was so sad. So, like where You can't I mean, these airplanes can't work at DCA, right? Can they work in San Diego, really? How far can they go from San Diego?
transcript.zh: 当时真是太让人遗憾了。所以……我的意思是，这批飞机在DCA（里根国家机场）是运营不了的，对吧？它们在圣迭戈真的能用吗？从圣迭戈起飞能飞多远？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: You're talking operationally.
transcript.zh: 你指的是运行层面上。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Well, operationally Oh, yeah, commercially, they can work from DCA, but I don't, you know, maybe not with 10 10 people on them because that's all you could fit. But so where where are these
transcript.zh: 额，运行层面……噢是的，从商业角度来看它们确实能飞DCA，但……额，只坐10名乘客可能还行，因为受限制大概也就只能装这么多了。所以，这些飞机到底要飞哪儿……

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Where's it realistically going to go? It looks like it's not Florida from the general vicinity of the map.
transcript.zh: 实际上它到底会飞哪儿？从地图上的大致方位看，应该不是佛罗里达。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: The glow didn't go that far down the East Coast. Yes.
transcript.zh: 光亮并没有延伸到东海岸那么靠南的地方。是的。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: No, it would be a super curveball if it was like Sarasota! Sarasota?
transcript.zh: 不，要是飞萨拉索塔那可真是个惊天大转折！萨拉索塔？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: No, give me something, please. I'm so... this is what I care about.
transcript.zh: 别这样，拜托透露一点吧。我太想知道了……我就关心这个。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: That was like the 10th version of those lines.
transcript.zh: 那张图上的航线大概改了有十版。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Was it? You guys...
transcript.zh: 是吗？你们可真行……

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Oh yeah, yeah. There were actually dots at one point.
transcript.zh: 对啊对啊。有一版上面甚至全都是点。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: There were just dots? Well, that was less of a tease if you just left it as dots.
transcript.zh: 全都是点？好吧，要是只留几个点，倒还没那么吊胃口。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I know. This was way better, just a glow down the East Coast.
transcript.zh: 我知道。现在这版好多了，只是沿着东海岸泛起一道光晕。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: All right. Well, come on, give me something.
transcript.zh: 行吧，别卖关子了，好歹透露一点嘛。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Look, look, look. They're going to fly California to New York, for sure, right? We know that.
transcript.zh: 听着听着，他们肯定会飞加州到纽约的航线，对吧？这点大家都清楚。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Right. This is the Project Gotham...
transcript.zh: 没错，这就是所谓的哥谭项目（Project Gotham）……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Congratulations, Albany. You win.
transcript.zh: 恭喜奥尔巴尼，你们赢了。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Yes, yes, yes. I'm not sure we're going to get one into Long Beach first, but you know, we'll get close.
transcript.zh: 是啊是啊。我不确定第一班会不会飞长滩，不过你知道，肯定八九不离十。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: If you do, you've really screwed up.
transcript.zh: 要是真飞长滩，那你们可真是搞砸了。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah. That's not going to happen. They're going to fly out of Seattle, for sure.
transcript.zh: 对对对，绝不可能发生那种事。他们肯定会从西雅图始发。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: We're not putting restrictions on them from a commercial perspective. Yeah, there are some... there's like two airports that they may not work on, just in terms of runway length and stuff like that.
transcript.zh: 从商业运营角度来看，我们并没有给他们设限。不过确实有那么一两个机场，受跑道长度等硬件条件限制，可能不太适合。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Is San Diego one of those?
transcript.zh: 圣迭戈是其中之一吗？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: You know, we'll see if we can find a spot for San Diego to fly them. They're going to be concentrated in California to New York, Seattle to the East Coast.
transcript.zh: 这个嘛，到时候看看能不能给圣迭戈挤出个机位吧。主要航线还是会集中在加州到纽约、西雅图到东海岸。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: But I wouldn't count out the idea that they could go the other direction and transit the ocean as well. Who knows? We'll see.
transcript.zh: 不过我也不排除反向飞行跨越大洋的可能性。谁知道呢？走着瞧吧。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Hawaii? Other direction?
transcript.zh: 夏威夷？反方向？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Like I said in my... It was... I'm surprised you didn't pick up. I had very intentional, prepared remarks in yesterday's script: they're going to go transcontinental or other markets where there's strong demand fit.
transcript.zh: 就像我昨天在发言稿里特意准备好的措辞一样——我很惊讶你居然没注意到——他们会执飞跨大陆航线，或者其他需求匹配度高的高客流市场。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Well, okay. Caracas starts when?
transcript.zh: 好吧，行吧。那加拉加斯航线什么时候开航？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Well, now you've got a branding problem, so how does that get resolved? This is a broader question, Brian. You probably want to get into this.
transcript.zh: 那现在你们就面临品牌定位的问题了，这该怎么解决呢？这是个更宏观的课题，Brian，你大概想聊聊这个吧。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Maybe later, but I want to just stay on the premium thing. So, Glen Hauenstein retired at Delta recently, and I was trying to get some information on his successor, Joe Esposito.
transcript.zh: 晚点再聊那个，我想先继续深挖高端定位这个话题。Delta 的 Glen Hauenstein 最近退休了，我正想打听一下他的继任者 Joe Esposito 的情况。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And I was talking to a source, I said, "What's he like?" And they said, "He's more aggressive than Glen," which kind of shocked me.
transcript.zh: 我跟一位消息人士聊了聊，问他：“这个人行事风格怎么样？”对方说：“他比 Glen 还要激进”，这让我颇感意外。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And then obviously, Patrick Quayle at United, very aggressive. I don't know if you remember what he did to you in San Diego with the triple seven.
transcript.zh: 另外显然，United 的 Patrick Quayle 也是极其强势进取。不知道你还记不记得他当年在圣迭戈用 777 是怎么阻击你们的。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And so, these airlines... Delta's big here, United's big, New York to California. Do you expect them to just let you waltz into these markets without pushing you around a lot?
transcript.zh: 所以面对这些巨头……Delta 在这里体量庞大，United 在纽约到加州航线上也实力雄厚。你难道指望他们会眼睁睁看着你们大摇大摆切入这些市场，而不对你们大打出手吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Like, how concerned are you that not just that they're going to compete, but they're going to do irrational things to mess with you? Because it's... there's a lot of testosterone in the industry.
transcript.zh: 换句话说，你有多担心他们不仅会正面竞争，甚至会采取一些非理性的杀敌一千自损八百的手段来整你们？毕竟这个行业向来充满了好斗的雄性荷尔蒙。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Yeah. Yeah.
transcript.zh: 确实，没错。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: You think it's smart for me to answer that question?
transcript.zh: 你觉得我现在回答这个问题明智吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Well, I'm sure... so Caylee, your PR person, is just to your left, and I know she's very good, and I'm sure that you have some sort of answer that you can give us.
transcript.zh: 呃，我相信……你看你们的公关 Caylee 就坐在你左手边，我知道她非常专业，所以我相信你肯定准备好了一套能向我们公开的外交辞令。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Look, we...
transcript.zh: 听我说，我们……

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: No, we don't presume anything about our competition. We don't presume that they are interested in our, in our strategy, or allowing us to go and do whatever we would like to do. We have been competing as aggressively and as hard as any airline in this industry in the 25 years I've been here. I don't think anybody's given us anything.
transcript.zh: 不，我们绝不会对竞争对手做任何想当然的预设。我们不指望他们会对我们的战略网开一面，或者放任我们随心所欲地扩张。在我入职的这25年里，我们的竞争策略与业内任何航司相比都同样激进、毫不手软。我认为从没有人给过我们任何施舍。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And we spent 15 years competing with the largest airline on the planet, and likely the most profitable on the planet. And we haven't lost market share, we haven't lost loyalty. We announced the international markets, we presumed that they would do something in their own network that they thought made sense for them. That really at the end of the day can't be what drives us.
transcript.zh: 过去15年里，我们一直在与全球规模最大、很可能也是盈利能力最强的航司正面交锋。我们没有丢掉市场份额，也没有失去旅客忠诚度。我们公布进军国际市场的计划时，就预料到他们会在其航线网络中采取自认为合理的反制动作。但归根结底，这绝不能成为左右我们发展的动因。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: We have to go earn the right to build loyalty, to serve our guests' demand, to give people reasons to choose us over them. That's like the beauty of this country and our system.
transcript.zh: 我们必须凭实力去争取旅客的忠诚，去满足客流需求，去给旅客充足的理由选择我们而非竞争对手。而这正是这个国家及其自由市场机制的魅力所在。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Can we shift long haul now?
transcript.zh: 我们现在能聊聊远程航线吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: All right, another way they can lose money. Let's go.
transcript.zh: 行啊，又多了一个亏钱的门道，来吧。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Let's go to long haul a little bit here. I want to talk about the joint venture a little bit here. So you may be familiar that Hawaiian tried to get one of those with JAL at one point. It did not happen, got shot down.
transcript.zh: 我们来稍微聊聊远程航线。我想谈谈航线联营（JV）的事。你们可能知道，夏威夷航空曾试图与日航（JAL）组建联营，但未能成行，被监管部门否决了。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: You're now trying to join with another domestic carrier to do both the trans-Pacific and trans-Atlantic. I guess not Qantas? Is that one not on the table? It's...
transcript.zh: 而你们现在正试图与另一家本土航司联手，同时布局跨太平洋和跨大西洋航线。我猜这里面不包括澳航吧？那家没在考虑范围内吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I hear the Australian regulator is pretty tough, huh?
transcript.zh: 听说澳大利亚的监管机构相当难搞，对吧？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Oh, maybe that's why.
transcript.zh: 哦，可能正是这个原因。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: That wasn't one we announced, no.
transcript.zh: 我们公布的名单里确实没有它。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Yeah. But, you know, this obviously would be huge for Alaska commercially to get into this. Can you really get this through? Is this something that is a factor of the climate in the US currently?
transcript.zh: 对。但你知道，涉足这一领域对阿拉斯加航空的商业发展显然意义重大。你们真的能推动其获批吗？这在多大程度上取决于当前美国的监管环境？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Or is this just something that you think there's a story that can be told that can get approved at any time here? And I guess, do you think you're going to have to have carve-outs or any sort of concessions to get this through? How are you viewing this new effort that you're about to embark on?
transcript.zh: 抑或你们认为只要给出一个合乎逻辑的由头，任何时候都能获批？而且我想知道，你们是否认为必须做出航线豁免剔除或某种让步妥协才能通关？你们如何看待即将展开的这项新动作？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I will address that. We are high on Honolulu to Australia. It's doing quite well.
transcript.zh: 我来回应一下这个问题。我们非常看好火奴鲁鲁至澳大利亚的航线，目前表现相当不错。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: I just flew it. Yeah, flew it in August.
transcript.zh: 我刚坐过，对，八月份坐的。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Thank you very much. Yes, thank you very much, Jon. And Andrew, who is obviously a native Australian, couldn't be happier about the recent improvement in that market, so we're excited about that.
transcript.zh: 非常感谢。是的，太感谢你了，Jon。Andrew 作为地道的澳大利亚人，对该市场近期的向好态势也是倍感振奋，所以我们对此充满期待。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I think, look, cannot obviously and will not get ahead of the regulatory process. It's there for a reason, a very important reason. We do think that at the end of the day this is about a level playing field, and we're bringing and wanting to bring more capacity...
transcript.zh: 我认为，听着，我们显然无法也绝不会去预判监管审批流程。监管的存在自有其非常重要的理由。但我们确实坚信，这归根结底是为了营造公平竞争的环境，而我们正在并将继续注入更多运力……

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: More choice, more competition into these markets. And that's really, I think, what underlies, ultimately, a lot of these discussions. We've got a long order book of new aircraft that we want to bring into Seattle and be able to place in many points internationally.
transcript.zh: 为这些市场带来更多选择和更充分的竞争。我认为这正是许多此类讨论的根本出发点。我们有很长的飞机储备订单，希望将新飞机引入西雅图，并投放至更多国际航点。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And in order to ensure that that is something that the market is able to support, we believe having the opportunity to participate in the same arrangement that every other airline who does this, a large airline who does this from the US, is the right right approach.
transcript.zh: 为了确保市场能够消化这部分运力，我们认为，争取与其他所有执飞此类航线的大型美国航司同等的合作机制，才是正确的途径。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And of course, it's something we would be wanting to pursue. And yes, of course, we have a level of confidence that it's possible. If we thought it wasn't possible, we probably wouldn't be talking about it at all. But it's a process, there's a long process ahead of us.
transcript.zh: 当然，这是我们极力追求的目标。而且我们也有相当的信心认为这是可行的。如果我们觉得不可能，根本就不会拿出来讨论。但这需要一个过程，前路漫漫。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: We're going to have to make the case for competition, which we'll do, and we're excited to be able to do that. But, yeah, we wouldn't have gone out today in the 8-K, a little earlier than we had anticipated, or at 1:00 p.m. in a joint release with our partners down at American if we thought there was not a decent chance that we would be able to ultimately obtain ATI.
transcript.zh: 我们需要陈述这有利于市场竞争的论据，我们也会全力以赴，且对此充满期待。如果觉得最终获得反垄断豁免（ATI）的希望不大，我们今天绝不会提前提交 8-K 文件，也不会在下午 1 点与合作伙伴美航联合发布公告。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: All right. But "a level playing field"—I feel like we've heard that before. Maybe in New York? Did someone talk about a level playing field?
transcript.zh: 好吧。但是“公平的竞争环境”——这话听着耳熟啊。是不是在纽约？之前有人提过“公平竞争环境”这词儿吧？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Are they going to call it the Northwest Alliance?
transcript.zh: 他们打算把它命名为“西北联盟”吗？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Ooh, that's what this is going to be? That was too soon?
transcript.zh: 噢，难道会是这个名字？这梗抛得太扎心了？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: NEA. NEA.
transcript.zh: NEA（东北联盟）。NEA。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: NEA, NEA, okay. Yes, the North... Okay.
transcript.zh: NEA，NEA，好吧。是的，东北……行。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: WCIA, that's a good model. It's a different model, very different model, yeah.
transcript.zh: 西海岸国际联盟，那倒是个好模版。不过模式截然不同，完全不同，是的。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Right. But I mean, obviously, if you were doing this as a US airline working with European and Pacific airlines, I don't think anyone would object to that, right? But you're doing this with another US-based airline, so that's what makes this different from everything else.
transcript.zh: 没错。但很显然，如果你是一家美国航司，与欧洲或太平洋对岸的航司合作，我觉得没人会反对，对吧？但你们这次是与另一家美国本土航司联手，这正是它的特殊之处。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Sure. Yeah, but that doesn't serve the market. So yeah, it's novel, it's unique, but there's a reason that it makes sense, because we're bringing new capacity to a market that that other partner wasn't serving, didn't have an interest to serve.
transcript.zh: 确实。但那样并不能满足该市场的需求。所以是的，这种模式很新颖、很独特，但它的合理性在于：我们是在向另一个合作伙伴未曾覆盖、也无意开拓的市场输送全新运力。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: I want to talk about airplanes.
transcript.zh: 我想聊聊飞机。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: I know. You keep saying that. Talk about airplanes.
transcript.zh: 我知道。你一直挂在嘴边。聊飞机呗。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Look at him! He's the one who buys them.
transcript.zh: 看他！他才是掏钱买飞机的人。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: So we are at Boeing right now. I think the one thing coming away from today's media day, I heard you talk about the context for which you see the future. Okay, the future is constrained. You need bigger airplanes to do that.
transcript.zh: 我们现在就在波音现场。今天媒体日下来，我听你阐述了对未来发展背景的判断。好的，未来受资源限制，因此你们需要更大的飞机。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: You want more space for premium. You've got a Sea-Tac that is ostensibly full. You've got a US airline market that is very full.
transcript.zh: 你们希望能留出更多两舱及超级经济舱空间。西雅图机场（Sea-Tac）表面上已接近饱和，整个美国航空客运市场也极度拥挤。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: When you look at the constraints that you're under and the things that you're prioritizing within your...
transcript.zh: 面对自身所承受的资源约束，以及你们在当前规划中所优先考虑的重点……

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: For fleet within, uh, within your strategy, what kind of airplane do you want them thinking about for their next airplane as they get going on this process, which is getting underway by, by all, by all accounts?
transcript.zh: 立足于你们的机队和战略，随着这个项目全面铺开——目前各方消息都表明它已经启动了——你希望他们为下一代飞机考虑什么样的机型？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Right. I think it's a really important question. And, um, I, I'm not an engineer. I've been in the industry a long time.
transcript.zh: 没错。我认为这是一个至关重要的问题。我不是工程师，但我投身这个行业很久了。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I think the 737 program writ large is one of the most successful aircraft programs ever in the history of aviation. I think the engines on that, on that program are the most successful engines in the history of aviation.
transcript.zh: 我认为波音737项目总体而言是航空史上最成功的飞机项目之一。而该项目所搭载的发动机，也是航空史上最成功的发动机。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Uh, we built a company based on that, that aircraft and our partnership with Boeing. Um, we're only here today because of how good that aircraft was.
transcript.zh: 正是依托这款机型以及与波音的合作，我们建立起了这家公司。我们今天能站在这里，完全归功于这款飞机的出色性能。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Um, yeah, I think that frequency in the future cannot be the way that we grow, um, in really constrained airport environments.
transcript.zh: 是的，我认为在未来，在极度受限的机场运营环境中，增加航班频次绝不可能再是我们实现增长的途径了。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I think totally, huge fan of what this administration is doing to modernize air traffic control and the way we route aircraft, uh, um, across the country. I think, I'm, and I'm hopeful.
transcript.zh: 我非常非常支持本届政府在空中交通管制现代化以及全国航路规划优化方面所做的努力。我对此充满希望。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I'm glad they got the first 12 billion. I want them to get the next 30. That's going to help everybody.
transcript.zh: 我很高兴他们拿到了第一笔120亿美元资金，我希望他们能再拿下接下来的300亿。这对所有人都是利好。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: We need to be able to, to run the airspace as efficiently as possible. But at the end of the day, in these really large cities, in really large markets, and that's becoming most of the industry, you've got to be able to get more gauge at, f- for each departure.
transcript.zh: 我们必须尽可能高效地运行这片空域。但归根结底，在这些特大城市、特大市场——这也正成为全行业的大势所趋——每个出发架次都必须能够提供更大的运载量（大机型）。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: As the economies grow, as population centers grow, and it does feel like populations continue to matriculate towards large cities and away from rural areas, um, the only way to answer that is, is with more density.
transcript.zh: 随着经济发展和人口中心壮大，而且看起来人口确实在持续涌向大城市、离开乡村地区，应对这一局面的唯一办法就是提高密度。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Um, I don't have a LOPA in mind. Jon, you probably, um, wake up at night with, uh, LOPAs on your mind for the next Boeing aircraft, uh, the, the NMA.
transcript.zh: 我脑子里倒没有具体的客舱布局（LOPA）。Jon，你半夜醒来可能脑子里都在琢磨波音下一代飞机（NMA）的客舱布局呢。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Um, but I think it's, look, whether they're ready to talk about it or not, um, as, as an airline, as, um, somebody who understands these are 10, 20, 30-year decisions, um, I think relatively soon, we need to start talking about what that next format should look like.
transcript.zh: 但我认为，不管他们现在愿不愿意讨论，作为一家航司，作为深知这些决定将影响未来10年、20年乃至30年的人，我认为在不久的将来，我们就必须开始探讨下一代机型应该是什么形态。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Um, and I think one of the most important parts of it is going to be we need new engine technology that works really, really well as well. Uh, this last round has had its struggles. We're all going through that.
transcript.zh: 而且我认为其中最核心的部分之一，就是需要同样非常非常出色的全新发动机技术。上一轮换代经历了不少挫折，我们现在都深陷其中。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Um, what, um, what the traveling public relies on and what airlines rely on are, and we took it for granted on some level, really, amazingly reliable airframes and engines.
transcript.zh: 出行公众和航空公司所依赖的，在某种程度上甚至被我们视为理所当然的，就是极其可靠的机体和发动机。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Um, we can worry about the rest. We can worry about whether premium's going to implode or, or blow up and be a great thing forever. Uh, we want to worry less about aircraft and engines over time.
transcript.zh: 剩下的事我们可以去操心。我们可以去担心两舱/溢价市场是会崩盘，还是会持续繁荣、永远向好。但长远来看，我们希望在飞机和发动机本身上少操点心。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I would love, you know, something in the, I don't know, 220 to 250 range ultimately. It's a long time off, but, yeah, I do think that that is the way that we're going to be able to grow over time, not through frequency.
transcript.zh: 最终我希望能有座级在220到250座左右的机型。虽然这还很遥远，但我确实认为，随着时间推移，我们将依靠这种方式实现增长，而不是单靠增加航班频次。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: It's just too hard to get all the departures at the same time of day because everybody wants to fly, strangely enough, kind of at the same time.
transcript.zh: 要在一天的同一时间段安排所有起飞架次实在太难了，因为奇怪的是，所有人几乎都想在同一个时间段出行。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Well, we had Ben Minicucci on the show in December of 2024 at your last big investor day, and he volunteered for us that engine overhauls were costing millions more than had been initially--
transcript.zh: 我们在2024年12月，也就是你们上次大型投资者日时请到了Ben Minicucci上节目。他主动向我们透露，发动机大修的成本比最初预期的多出了数百万——

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Is that a quote? Direct quote. Direct quote, yes. Well, you know, you've got the spreadsheet. I do, yeah. Yeah.
transcript.zh: 这是原话吗？原话，千真万确。好吧，你手里有财务数据表。确实有，是的。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Well, okay, so what was really fascinating about that, I thought, was that it spoke to the arrangement that airframers have with engine makers and engine makers have with airlines. As you think about this next product, how do you want the relationship with engine makers to evolve?
transcript.zh: 好吧，我认为这件事真正引人深思的地方在于，它反映了飞机制造商与发动机制造商之间，以及发动机厂商与航司之间的合作模式。展望下一代产品时，你希望与发动机制造商的关系如何演进？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: You know, obviously, you're going to be carrying a lot of risk with an all-new aircraft, an all-new engine. What should that balance be as far as what the business model needs to be for you to feel comfortable, given all the lessons learned from this round with engines, which has been unbelievably expensive and painful?
transcript.zh: 显然，采用全新飞机和全新发动机要承担巨大的风险。考虑到这轮发动机问题带来了极其高昂的成本和惨痛的教训，为了让你们感到放心，商业模式的平衡点应该落在哪里？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Yeah. I mean, I'll just say it. I think choice is important. At the end of the day, I think competition is always helpful and beneficial to everybody.
transcript.zh: 是的。我就直说了吧，我认为选择权非常重要。归根结底，竞争对所有人来说都是有益且有帮助的。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: It makes the people who are competing for the business better at what they do, and it gives those who are, you know, on the other end buying equipment, you know, more choice as well. Look, having-- I'll reiterate, the 737, the CFM56 were like engineering marvels, and we built an entire business around that model.
transcript.zh: 它能促使竞标方不断精进自身业务，同时也让采购设备的买方拥有更多选择。听着，我再重申一遍，737和CFM56发动机简直就是工程学奇迹，我们围绕这一机型建立起了整个商业模式。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I just think as we all push on the capabilities of the current technology that we have, the current materials that we have, it's just think it's important when we sit down and we look at how we want to build a strategy over a 20 or 30-year life cycle of an aircraft, that we want to make sure that people are really competing hard to give us their very best product at all times.
transcript.zh: 我认为，当我们不断挑战现有技术和现有材料的极限时，在坐下来规划飞机20至30年生命周期的战略时，非常重要的一点就是要确保各家厂商全力竞争，始终为我们提供他们最优秀的产品。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And I think there's an argument that you might want more sort of diversity in your pool. Just, if one thing goes wrong with the one thing that you buy, it's really problematic to your strategy.
transcript.zh: 而且我认为有理由在机队池中保持更多的多样性。否则，如果你采购的单一款型出了问题，就会对你的整体战略造成极大的麻烦。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: And which do you get first, a new Boeing airplane or a new Sea-Tac terminal?
transcript.zh: 那么你会先迎来哪一个：波音的新飞机，还是西雅图-塔科马机场的新航站楼？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: New Sea-Tac terminal. We just built new Sea-Tac terminals, and we're going to go and renovate another one. So, it's a beautiful airport. Do you think, Jon? You live here.
transcript.zh: 西雅图-塔科马机场的新航站楼。我们刚建好了西塔机场的新航站区，接下来还要翻新另一个。这机场很漂亮，你觉得呢，Jon？你住在这儿。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: I do spend a lot of time there. No, look, I think it's-- I'm psyched about the Chili's.
transcript.zh: 我确实在那儿待了很长时间。不，看吧，我觉得——我对那家Chili's餐厅挺满意的。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Are you surprised?
transcript.zh: 你觉得意外吗？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: That there was a Chili's? Yeah. I don't know if I was surprised by it, but, you know, it's like...
transcript.zh: 你说那里有家 Chili's？对啊。我倒不觉得有多意外，不过，你知道的，就感觉……

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: How is this a thing? This is like the fifth time this has come up in the last two days. What is wrong with you people here?
transcript.zh: 这怎么还能成个话题了？过去两天这已经是第五次聊到它了。你们这群人到底怎么回事？

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: We get very excited in the Pacific Northwest about... It's like, yeah. Yeah.
transcript.zh: 我们太平洋西北地区的人一旦遇到……对，就是这样。没错。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: About Chili's? This is okay, it's very confusing.
transcript.zh: 为了一家 Chili's 兴奋？这……好吧，真是让人摸不着头脑。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Full every time I go by it.
transcript.zh: 每次我路过那儿都是爆满。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: That's amazing. Thank you to Straightaway Cocktails, by the way. We really do appreciate that.
transcript.zh: 真是绝了。顺便感谢 Straightaway Cocktails 提供的鸡尾酒，我们由衷感谢。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Can I just point out to the listeners, 'cause this is going to go on the internet, I'm the only person on the stage here not drinking hard alcohol, so I'm missing some of the jokes. Shane, would you like a rare-for-me softball question? 'Cause I am kind of fascinated by this.
transcript.zh: 我能不能跟听众们说明一下，因为这期节目要发到网上——我是台上唯一一个没喝烈酒的人，所以我有些梗都没接上。Shane，你想回答一个由我提出的难得一见的温和问题吗？因为我对这事儿挺着迷的。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Gird yourself.
transcript.zh: 做好心理准备。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: You're not the first person to have the role of president and CFO, but it is somewhat rare at an airline. And one reason I think it might be somewhat rare at an airline or any company, is as a president, part of your job is revenue and premium trends.
transcript.zh: 你不是第一个同时兼任总裁兼首席财务官的人，但在航空公司里这确实不多见。我认为在航司或任何企业中这种情况不多的一个原因在于：作为总裁，你的部分职责是关注收入以及高端客舱的趋势。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: And I would imagine also as CFO, part of your job is to say, that costs how much? Did you have this like weird experience where like the revenue guy in you wanted to approve things for what you were announcing today, and the CFO was like, oh my god? And then, was there anything that at the end of the day, like, your product team wanted, and you were like, enough?
transcript.zh: 我猜作为 CFO，你的另一半职责则是质问：“那得花多少钱？！”你有没有过这种古怪的撕裂体验：内心负责收入的那个你很想批准今天宣布的这些项目，而 CFO 身份的你却直呼“我的天呐”？到头来，有没有什么产品团队想要的东西，被你一口回绝说“够了”？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: We're not doing it.
transcript.zh: “这事儿免谈。”

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Yeah.
transcript.zh: 对。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: This is what I wake up in the middle of the night with cold sweats on. What did I say yes to? The pizza oven, really? Yeah, yeah, yeah.
transcript.zh: 这就是半夜让我惊出一身冷汗的噩梦。我到底点头答应了些什么？披萨烤箱，真要上这个？是啊，是啊。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: You approved the pizza oven.
transcript.zh: 你还真批了披萨烤箱。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: You know, there are definitely things we say no to. And...
transcript.zh: 你懂的，有些东西我们坚决说“不”。而且……

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: Like screens?
transcript.zh: 比如机载屏幕？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Like screens, Brett. Like screens. Yes, no. No to screens. Yes.
transcript.zh: 比如屏幕，Brett。比如屏幕。对，不行。屏幕坚决不行，确实。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: There are things we say no to. Ben sort of mentioned it today. This evolution wasn't an easy evolution. I think our first sort of like, can we do premium but like really cheap, and get like all of the yield, but like not really invest? You can't do it that way. You've got to put a really high-quality product out there.
transcript.zh: 确实有些东西我们拒绝了。Ben 今天也提到了这一点。这种转型绝非易事。我想我们最初的念头是：能不能既做高端服务又把成本压得极低，既赚取所有的收益率（Yield）又不用真正投入？但根本走不通。你必须拿出真正高品质的产品。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And the one thing, like, we talked to our people about this, if you're going to be in this industry, most people who come to this industry, you devote your whole life to it. So you've got to love kind of what you're doing, what you're trying to do. And what you're really trying to do is give people a really good experience.
transcript.zh: 还有一点，我们也常和员工聊起：如果你要投身这个行业——大多数进入民航业的人往往会奉献一生——你就必须热爱自己的本职工作，热爱你的目标。而我们真正的目标，就是为旅客提供极为出色的体验。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And I've made my peace with, like, we are going to invest in the experience for people.
transcript.zh: 我也彻底想通了：我们就是要大力投资，提升旅客的出行体验。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I thought what you were trying to do is get to $10 in EPS.
transcript.zh: 我还以为你的目标是把每股收益（EPS）做到 10 美元呢。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: That's going to happen. Turns out that if you give people a really good experience, they give you enough fare that you can get to $10 a share. Turns out.
transcript.zh: 那是一定会实现的。事实证明，只要你给旅客提供真正优质的体验，他们就会支付足够高的票价，支撑你实现每股 10 美元的目标。事实就是如此。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Okay. All right.
transcript.zh: 行吧，好吧。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Have you talked to your soon-to-be joint venture partner about this?
transcript.zh: 关于这点，你跟你们即将结成联营（JV）的合作伙伴聊过了吗？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: They're making great moves down there, have you not been watching?
transcript.zh: 他们在那边的大动作可不少，难道你没关注吗？

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: I've been watching, Brett. Do you want to go in this direction? They're putting screens back on.
transcript.zh: 我一直在关注啊，Brett。你想聊这个方向吗？他们又把机载屏幕装回去了。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Oh, no, I have been watching, absolutely. Look, I am curious though about the screen thing, not because of screens, but because a lot of what you announced today felt like a we're trying to be competitive, be on the same level playing field with the rest of the global premium carriers, as they like to call themselves, right? But one of the differentiators is you're not putting screens on the domestic fleet, and even on the Max 10, on the Aurora, whatever you, I don't know what you're calling the back of those things.
transcript.zh: 噢不，我确实一直在关注。不过我对屏幕这事挺好奇的，倒不是因为屏幕本身，而是因为你们今天宣布的很多内容，感觉都像是在努力保持竞争力，和自称全球高端航司的其他同行站在同一起跑线上，对吧？但一个差异化之处在于，你们并没有在境内机队上加装屏幕，甚至连 MAX 10 上、极光舱后面的——我不知道你们怎么称呼那后面的区域。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: The back of the Aurora Suite airplanes? The marketing team will come back to you soon.
transcript.zh: 配备极光套房客舱飞机的后舱？市场团队很快就会给你答复的。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: The point is though, like this is a notable difference between what other airlines have done, including American. You talk about them doing great things down there lately, but they recently made the decision that they need screens. So was this sort of the limit for you, where you hit this wall?
transcript.zh: 但关键在于，这与其他航司的做法有着显著不同，包括美航。你们刚还提到他们最近成绩斐然，但他们最近决定必须装屏幕。所以这对你们来说算是一个底线、撞到的一道墙吗？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: No, it's way less exciting than that. Really, it's, look, we announced a lot today, and we announced a lot of investment. And the decision was made easy because the time to market with that is so long that fortunately, I didn't have to make a hard decision.
transcript.zh: 不，实际情况远没有那么戏剧化。说真的，你看，我们今天宣布了很多内容，宣布了大量的投资。而这个决定其实很容易做，因为推向市场的周期实在太长了，所以幸运的是，我根本不需要去做什么艰难的抉择。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: It was an easy decision, it just takes too long to do it. I don't know what we would have decided if you could tell me we could get, you know, approval and certification on a seat tomorrow, and we could get through it very, very quickly. I'm not sure. We didn't have to face that just because the length is too long.
transcript.zh: 这是个容易的决定，因为耗时实在太长了。我也不知道如果我们明天就能拿到某款座椅的适航认证和取证、能以极快速度推进的话我们会怎么决定。我不确定。我们之所以不用纠结这个，纯粹是因为周期太长。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: We need to get the full sort of remodel of the airplanes done, the full extension of the premium experience done, we're hoping by, you know, '28, so we can realize a full year of the benefits of that in '29 and beyond. I also think, and we've learned a lot, Starlink is, I don't know if you've flown with it, it is pretty frickin' remarkable.
transcript.zh: 我们需要把客舱全面改装完成，将高端体验全面铺开，我们希望能在 2028 年前搞定，这样我们就能在 2029 年及以后充分享受一整年的成效。另外我认为，而且我们也了解到了很多——星链（Starlink），我不知道你们体验过没有，它简直太惊艳了。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Yeah, I have. Oh, I flew on Hawaiian, it's amazing.
transcript.zh: 我有过。噢，我坐夏威夷航空体验过，太不可思议了。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I think you guys may have mentioned this or written about it. It's remarkable. We had a customer panel at our annual planning session with our officers, which we did at the same, we're actually at a local hotel, but we've had them at the same training center as well. And they didn't talk about screens.
transcript.zh: 我想你们可能提过或写过这事。确实非常出色。我们之前在与高管举行的年度规划会议上组织了一次客户座谈会，那次是在当地一家酒店，不过我们之前在培训中心也办过。他们完全没提屏幕的事。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: They did talk about free internet, reliable internet, internet that doesn't go down, and internet that lets them stream their own content. So we'll see if it becomes a big product gap. I think our hypothesis is that maybe it won't be, because we're going to give people free Starlink.
transcript.zh: 他们确实谈到了免费网络、可靠的网络、不掉线的网络，以及能让他们串流播放自己内容的网络。所以我们会观察这是否会演变成明显的产品差距。我认为我们的假设是它可能不会，因为我们要给大家提供免费的星链。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I will tell you the first time, and we said yes to it, but the first time they brought the Starlink business case to me, I had that
transcript.zh: 我得告诉你，第一次——虽然我们最终批准了——但当他们第一次把星链的商业可行性方案呈报给我时，我也有过那种

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: ...reaction, Jon, that you were sort of like miming? And then I thought maybe I could go change the entire revenue model of Starlink and have them allow us to maybe charge for the service?
transcript.zh: ……Jon，就像你刚刚比划出的那个反应？然后我想，也许我能去改变星链的整个收益模式，让他们允许我们对这项服务收费？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: Turns out, no. The people who run Starlink don't care about what I have to say about the revenue model. And so look, here we are. We are offering free internet to everybody, which I'm glad about. At the end of the day, it's the right thing to do.
transcript.zh: 结果证明不行。负责星链的人根本不在乎我对收益模式有什么看法。所以你看，事实就是这样，我们正在向所有人提供免费机上网络，我对此感到很高兴。归根结底，这是正确的做法。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And it's a great experience for guests, and our Net Promoter Scores on the flights and equipment that have Starlink are meaningfully higher than the ones that don't, just for that fact that they have Starlink, amazingly enough.
transcript.zh: 这对旅客来说是很棒的体验，而且令人惊讶的是，仅仅因为配备了星链，搭载该设备的机型和航班净推荐值（NPS）就显著高于未配备的航班。

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: Well, look, okay. Lightning round, one question. What Okay, you can't say NPS. What is the most underappreciated metric in all of your time as CFO for what makes an airline an airline?
transcript.zh: 好吧，快问快答环节，就一个问题。在你不准说 NPS 的前提下，在你担任首席财务官的所有岁月里，用来衡量航空公司本质的最被低估的指标是什么？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: This is the lightning round? I need like 10 minutes to think about this question! The one metric...
transcript.zh: 这叫快问快答？我得花上十分钟才能想清楚这个问题！最关键的一个指标……

transcript.speaker: Brian Sumers
transcript.en: The metric, yeah. What's the underappreciated metric that you really rely on and you don't think is... Yeah, no, NPS doesn't count.
transcript.zh: 对，就是那个指标。哪项被低估的指标是你真正看重，却觉得外界没有给予足够关注的？没错，NPS 不能算。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: But I can't say You've already told me what I cannot... Does it have to be a piece of data that comes to me on a spreadsheet?
transcript.zh: 但不能说……你已经限定了我不能提什么……这必须是表格上呈现给我的某项具体数据吗？

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: There was once a guy who said that as long as the plane leaves on time, the food tastes better, what else?
transcript.zh: 曾经有人说过，只要飞机准点起飞，机上餐食吃起来都更香，还有别的吗？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I think that's all true, but I mean, no joke, and I know you guys don't like this sappy stuff, but I'm emotionally connected to this industry and this company. And the thing that matters the most when we hear from guests who write to us—and we get lots of emails when people have bad experiences or tough experiences...
transcript.zh: 我认为这些都没错，但说真的——我知道你们不爱听这些煽情的话——我对这个行业和这家公司有着深厚的感情。当听到给我们写信的旅客心声时，最触动人心的莫过于此——虽然旅客遇到糟糕或坎坷的经历时我们也会收到大量邮件……

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: He points at me.
transcript.zh: 他指着我呢。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: But we more often than I would have ever expected to hear, hear from guests that they felt like they were at home when they come on our airline. That's the only reason we have loyalty. It's the only reason people always want to come back to us.
transcript.zh: 但我们听到旅客说登上我们的飞机就像回家一样的频率，远远超出了我的预期。这是我们能够收获忠诚度的唯一原因，也是大家总想再次选择我们的唯一理由。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: It's the reason they choose us over people who want to come in from other parts of the world and declare that this is, you know, a market that they're going to own. And so we don't have that on a spreadsheet, but that's really, ultimately, I think that expression is what matters the most and it's what drives loyalty.
transcript.zh: 这也是面对那些从世界其他地方杀过来、扬言要占领这片市场的竞争对手时，旅客依然选择我们的原因。虽然这种感受无法体现在数据表格上，但归根结底，我认为旅客的这份认可才是最重要的，也是维系忠诚度的根本动力。

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: And it's really what our people, without anything that we ask them to do from the corporate headquarters, just deliver every single day.
transcript.zh: 而这正是我们的员工即便没有任何来自公司总部的硬性要求，也始终日复一日践行并呈现出来的。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Just one last one for you. Which do you miss more, the carpets on the bulkhead walls or the prayer cards?
transcript.zh: 最后再问你一个问题。隔框舱壁上的地毯挂饰和祈祷卡，你更怀念哪一个？

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: I appreciate the history of both of those and why they existed in the moment in time they did. But I was quite partial to the tapestry, which we referred to it as, and by the way, one of the very...
transcript.zh: 我非常尊重这两者的历史底蕴，以及它们在特定历史时期存在的意义。但我个人更偏爱那种我们称之为挂毯的装饰。顺便提一句，这确实是……

transcript.speaker: Shane Tackett
transcript.en: The last tapestries that came off of an aircraft was gifted to our former CEO, Bill Ayer. And it does occupy space on his aircraft, his personal aircraft that I think is a Cessna or something that he flies around every once in a while.
transcript.zh: 飞机上拆下的最后几块壁毯赠给了我们的前任首席执行官 Bill Ayer。现在就挂在他的飞机上，是他平时偶尔开着兜风的私人飞机，好像是一架塞斯纳什么的。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Shane Tackett, thank you for joining us on The Air Show podcast.
transcript.zh: Shane Tackett，非常感谢你做客 The Air Show 播客。

transcript.speaker: Brett Snyder
transcript.en: You've been listening to The Air Show. If you have suggestions or questions for us, or are interested in sponsoring the podcast, email us at info@theairshowpodcast.com to get in touch.
transcript.zh: 您正在收听的是 The Air Show。如果您有任何建议、问题，或有意赞助本节目，请发送邮件至 info@theairshowpodcast.com 与我们联系。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: Now we do have a few thank-yous here. Again, thank you Leo for producing this, coming up from LA. We appreciate this. Thank you to Graham who is here, and Andrew who is not, from Bullpen Strategies, who put this all together. Thank you guys so much.
transcript.zh: 现在我们还要表达几声感谢。再次感谢专程从洛杉矶赶来负责现场制作的 Leo，非常感谢你。还要感谢亲自到场的 Graham 以及未能前来的 Andrew，他们来自负责统筹这一切的 Bullpen Strategies。非常感谢你们二位。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: And thank you to Boeing for the space, and Teague for putting this all together. We really appreciate that. And thank you Shane for coming here, and thank you to Alaska for helping make this whole thing possible with the media and investor day.
transcript.zh: 感谢波音提供场地，感谢 Teague 为组织本次活动所做的一切，我们铭记在心。感谢 Shane 的出席，也感谢阿拉斯加航空借助本次媒体与投资者日让这一切成为可能。

transcript.speaker: Jon Ostrower
transcript.en: It was a very long day and I'm sure Shane would like to go to bed now. But our theme music is by Joshua Mosier. Thanks for listening, and we'll be back soon.
transcript.zh: 今天真是漫长的一天，我肯定 Shane 现在只想赶紧去睡一觉。本节目片头音乐由 Joshua Mosier 创作。感谢收听，我们很快再见。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 独特卖点；惯用伎俩 / 招牌噱头
vocab_notes.note_zh: 源自意第绪语，在商业口语中常指某家品牌用来吸引眼球、区别于竞品的特色招牌卖点或噱头（如贵宾室提供现烤披萨或特色奶酪师）。
金融常客领域指利用不同支付清算渠道（如借记卡与信用卡刷卡手续费 interchange fee 上限法规）的费率差异来实现利润最大化。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 子机队（特定客舱构型的专属机队分支）
vocab_notes.note_zh: 指同一大类机型中经专门客舱改造、用于特定特殊航线市场（如专门配备全平躺商务舱执飞跨陆 transcon 航线）的一小批飞机集合。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 收益破坏；客公里收益暴跌
vocab_notes.note_zh: 民航收益管理术语，指当航司在某航线上大幅增投高端舱位运力导致供过于求，不得不通过降价促销，破坏整体平均票价收益率的现象。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 8-K 表格（美国上市公司重大事件临时报告）
vocab_notes.note_zh: 美国证券交易委员会（SEC）要求上市公司在发生重大合作、并购或战略变更等非定期重大事件时，必须在规定时限内向市场披露的临时公告。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 换用大机型；提升单机座级
vocab_notes.note_zh: 航线网络规划术语，指在时刻受限（slot-constrained）繁忙机场无法增加航班班次时，改用座位数更多、载客量更大的飞机以实现客流运力增长。
适航工程与客舱设计专业术语，指经民航适航当局批准的包含座椅间距、紧急出口、应急设备配置及厨房洗手间位置的客舱工程布局蓝图。

vocab_notes.meaning_zh: 新中型客机（波音未落地的中运量新机型代号）
vocab_notes.note_zh: 波音长期探讨用于填补 737 MAX 与 787 之间（约 220-270 座级跨大陆市场）的新一代中运量窄体/小型宽体飞机研发项目代号。
